pr_title: Feature(pr-review): defer slow registered tests out of fixer waves
verdict: READY TO MERGE - 12 of 12 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: The three new tests.* keys (timings, fixer_test_seconds, defer_flags) match defaults.json, the TestsConfig dataclass and builder in config.py, and the README key table, so the four-place contract holds.

fixer_test_seconds uses exclusiveMinimum 0 with a null escape, and the schema's number type rejects booleans, which fits the builder's float() conversion and the documented null means no runtime rule.
Schema descriptions agree with the README rows and the dataclass docstring, and the path-valued key reuses the relPath definition that rejects absolute paths.
_TIMINGS splits test_slow.py into 50 s + 40 s rows, each under the 60 s ceiling, so the brief test pins summing per file rather than per-row comparison.
The no-reach closeout test edits only docs/a.md after build while the PR itself changed src/pkg/a.py, proving deferred tests are scoped to what the fixes touched, not to the PR diff.
All new driver tests run the real waves/closeout CLI or the real defer_reasons over a real registry and timings file; no helper under test is stubbed.
`[run] = _run_lines(out)` asserts exactly one combined pytest command at closeout, and the brief test checks every run line names only the fast test.
test_config covers default, override (including float coercion) and four schema rejections for the three new tests keys.

The new tests.timings / fixer_test_seconds / defer_flags keys land in all four required places (defaults.json, harness.schema.json, the TestsConfig dataclass and _tests builder, the README key table), and the schema's exclusiveMinimum keeps the float() conversion safe.
file_seconds degrades to an empty map when the timings report is missing, unreadable or malformed, and rejects boolean durations, so a bad report never blocks wave planning.
Splitting _registry_rows out of registry_entries lets defer_reasons read the raw entries for flag lookup while existing callers keep the same (file, targets) tuples.

The fixer rule text ('Never run a test marked deferred ... closeout lists it') matches SKILL.md and operating_rules.md, and pytest_command keeps one place that builds both the per-test and the batched closeout commands.
The new config keys land in all four places CLAUDE.md requires (defaults.json, harness.schema.json, TestsConfig/_tests, README key table) with matching defaults (null, null, []).
The brief marker text 'deferred, do not run' is spelled identically in pr_review.py _tests_block, pr-fixer.md and SKILL.md Rule 2, so the fixer agent can match it literally.
pr-fixer.md states the deferred test stays in the file set and is editable, matching waves (deferral only changes the brief's test line, not the widened file set).
Step 8 instructs carrying the deferred block verbatim into the terminal summary, so unrun slow tests cannot silently disappear from the developer's view.

The three new tests.* keys land in all four places CLAUDE.md requires (defaults.json, schema, TestsConfig builder, README table) with matching null/[] defaults and schema guards (exclusiveMinimum, relPath, non-empty strings) that test_config.py exercises.
Splitting _registry_rows out of registry_entries lets defer_reasons read flags without changing registry_entries' contract for widened_waves and tests_for.

Driver tests are behavioral end to end: real registry and timings files through waves and closeout, a summed-over-the-ceiling case (50 + 40 > 60), a flagged-but-fast case, and a negative closeout case.
Deferred tests stay in the file set and the brief names each one with its reason, so a fixer can still edit a slow test without being invited to run it.
pytest_command centralizes the run-command string so brief lines and the closeout command cannot drift.

important.name: A configured runtime ceiling switches itself off without a word
important.summary:
file_seconds returns {} when tests.timings is missing, unparseable or holds no usable rows, and defer_reasons then defers by flags only; waves prints nothing about it, and test_unusable_timings_defer_by_flags_only pins the silence as the design. The likely trigger is mundane: a generated, gitignored timings report does not exist in a fresh worktree, so a project that set fixer_test_seconds gets fixers running the 20-minute suite the feature exists to keep out, and nobody is told. The feature's whole value rides on a file whose absence is invisible.

Also (runtime): defer_reasons formats the measured sum with `:.0f` and the ceiling with `:g` (line 1582). A file that sums to 30.4 s against a 30 s ceiling is deferred with the reason 'measured 30 s > 30 s'. A fractional ceiling gives similar output, e.g. 0.6 s against 0.5 s prints 'measured 1 s > 0.5 s'. This reason goes into fixer briefs and the closeout block, so it reads as a contradiction.

Also (roast): The comparison is strict on floats but the reason rounds with :.0f, so 60.4 s against a 60 s ceiling renders `measured 60 s > 60 s`, which reads like an off-by-one in the deferral rule.
fix: In _cmd_waves, when tests.fixer_test_seconds is set and file_seconds(repo) is empty, print one line such as `deferral: tests.timings <path> missing or unusable; runtime ceiling inactive (flags only)` next to the held line, and add a driver test asserting it.
Treat a configured fixer_test_seconds with a missing or unreadable tests.timings report as a CaptureError from waves naming the path, so the developer regenerates the report or nulls the ceiling.
Format the measured value with the same precision as the ceiling, e.g. `f"measured {seconds[test]:.1f} s > {ceiling:g} s"`.
Format the measured value with `{seconds[test]:.1f}` (or `:g`) in defer_reasons and update the driver test's expected `(measured 90 s > 60 s)` string accordingly.

important.name: No-ceiling test drops defer_flags, so flags-only deferral is never covered
important.summary:
test_no_ceiling_ignores_timings sets both fixer_test_seconds=None and defer_flags=[] and asserts {}. An early `if ceiling is None: return {}` in defer_reasons (pr_review.py:1572-1585) would still pass, silently disabling deferral for projects that configure only defer_flags (the shape most projects without a timings report will use). No other test exercises the flag branch with ceiling None; test_unusable_timings_defer_by_flags_only always runs with ceiling 60.

Also (tests): file_seconds rejects a bool duration (`not isinstance(duration, bool)`, pr_review.py:1559) and _read_json raises on a non-object top level, which file_seconds catches (pr_review.py:1551-1554). Neither a `"duration": true` row nor a top-level JSON list is in the parameter set, so removing either guard (a bool counting as 1.0 s, or an uncaught error on a list report) stays green.

Also (tests): Lines 3-4 state each test gets a copy of pr_template or its own _make_pr build. The new test_unusable_timings_defer_by_flags_only and test_no_ceiling_ignores_timings build bare projects with make_project and call activate(load_config(...)) directly (as TestConfigCommand already did), contradicting the stated contract.
fix: Keep defer_flags from _DEFER_TESTS (override only fixer_test_seconds=None) and assert script.defer_reasons(repo) == {"tests/test_flagged.py": "properties.super_slow"}: test_slow.py (90 s measured) staying absent proves timings are ignored, test_flagged.py present proves flags still apply.
Add a second parametrized case (ceiling None, flags kept) alongside the existing empty-flags case.
Add `{"tests": [{"file": "tests/test_slow.py", "duration": True}]}` and `[{"file": "tests/test_slow.py", "duration": 90}]` to the `timings` parametrize list.
Extend the module docstring: unit-level tests of driver functions (defer_reasons, config) build a bare project with make_project and activate its config directly.

minor.name: README tests.timings row omits the path-matching rule and silent no-op cases
minor.summary: README.md line 98 says the timings report's tests rows carry file and duration, summed per file, but defer_reasons matches seconds.get(test) by exact string against the registry entry's file, so a timings file spelled differently (absolute, backslashes, pytest nodeid) defers nothing without any message; file_seconds also swallows a missing or unreadable report (CaptureError -> {}), so a configured fixer_test_seconds silently has no effect. The schema description says repo-relative; the README, the one place users configure from, does not. Stock pytest JSON reports key rows by nodeid with per-phase durations, so the non-standard shape is easy to miss.
fix: Amend README.md line 98 to: 'a JSON report whose `tests` rows carry `file` (repo-relative POSIX, spelled as in the registry) and `duration` (seconds), summed per file; missing or unreadable means no runtime deferral'.

minor.name: 'It stays in the file set' is not always true
minor.summary: _tests_block lists tests_for every path in the fixer's file set, including paths widened in because a fix option names them, but review_merge._widening adds only registry tests targeting the part files. A deferred test reached only through a named path is listed as `deferred, do not run` yet is not in the file set, while pr-fixer.md and SKILL.md promise it is editable; a fixer that edits it trips closeout's file-set validation.
fix: Reword pr-fixer.md lines 46-48 and SKILL.md line 774 to 'editable when the file set lists it'.
Or widen review_merge._widening to add registry tests targeting the named fix paths too, so the claim holds.

minor.name: Module docstring omits the deferred-test behavior of waves and closeout and the new tests.* keys
minor.summary: The pr_review.py module docstring is the CLI contract. The `waves` entry (lines 48-56) does not say fixer briefs mark deferred tests 'do not run'. The `closeout` entry (lines 60-69) still ends at 'print the canonical Phase 5 line', but _cmd_closeout (1833-1835) now prints a `deferred tests:` block after it. The 'Project and paths' paragraph (84-89) names only `tests.registry` as the source of registry tests and leaves out `tests.timings`, `tests.fixer_test_seconds` and `tests.defer_flags`, which defer_reasons now reads. SKILL.md line 40 already documents the closeout block, so the driver's own docstring is the only place that disagrees.
fix: Add to the `waves` entry: registered tests that defer_reasons selects (summed tests.timings seconds over tests.fixer_test_seconds, or a true tests.defer_flags path) appear in the brief as 'deferred, do not run' with their reason; add to the `closeout` entry: then prints a `deferred tests:` block (each file, its reason, one pytest command) for deferred tests the paths changed since build_head reach; extend the 'Project and paths' sentence to name tests.timings, tests.fixer_test_seconds and tests.defer_flags.

minor.name: Timing rows match only an exact registry path
minor.summary: file_seconds keys seconds by row['file'] verbatim and defer_reasons looks them up by the registry's file string. A report keyed per test (`tests/test_x.py::test_y`), written with Windows backslashes, or prefixed `./` never matches, so the ceiling silently never fires; the README calls the rows per-test ('summed per file') without saying the file must equal the registry entry character for character.
fix: Normalize before summing: key = row['file'].replace('\', '/').split('::', 1)[0], strip a leading './'; add a parametrized case to test_unusable_timings_defer_by_flags_only's neighbour covering a nodeid-style and a backslash row.
State in the README tests.timings row and the schema description that `file` must equal the registry entry's `file` exactly.

minor.name: closeout computes deferred_lines after the commit, so a registry read error can hide the closeout problems
minor.summary:
_cmd_closeout calls deferred_lines (1834) after commit_review, after closeout.json is written and after save_plan. deferred_lines reads the registry through _registry_rows -> _read_json, which raises CaptureError on a malformed or non-object registry file. A fixer can edit the registry when a fix option names it, so this can happen. When it does, the review and the closeout marker are already written, the `raise CaptureError(problems)` at 1837 never runs, and stderr shows only the registry error, not the closeout problems that phase5_line just counted. Separately, line 1834 calls changed_paths(repo, build_head) a second time: closeout_review already ran it at 1845, so the three git calls run twice.

Also (roast): _cmd_closeout writes CLOSEOUT_MARK, saves the plan and prints the Phase 5 line before deferred_lines reads the registry. A registry a fixer broke (it can sit in a file set via a named fix path) makes _read_json raise there, so the run prints `Phase 5 [done]` and then exits non-zero, contradicting SKILL.md Step 8 ('closeout prints it only on exit 0'). It also recomputes changed_paths, two more git calls for data closeout_review already had.
fix: Compute the deferred block before commit_review: have closeout_review return the (changed, created) it already computed, build `deferred = deferred_lines(repo, changed | created)` in _cmd_closeout before the write, and only print it after phase5_line.
Or wrap the deferred_lines call so that a CaptureError becomes one extra problem appended to `problems` instead of replacing them.

Compute the deferred lines before _write_json(run / CLOSEOUT_MARK, ...), passing in the `changed` set closeout_review already computed (return it alongside the doc), and print them after the Phase 5 line.
Wrap the deferred_lines call in try/except CaptureError and print a single `deferred tests: registry unreadable (...)` line instead of raising.

minor.name: Closeout recomputes deferral from the current timing report instead of retaining what the fixer was told to skip.
minor.summary: Copilot (pullrequestreview-5556332749): Closeout recomputes deferral from the current timing report instead of retaining what the fixer was told to skip. If a targeted test run replaces that report with only its own results, a runtime-deferred test without a matching defer flag disappears from closeout, even when its target was edited and the test never ran. Persist the deferred tests and reasons when generating waves, preserve them across follow-up waves, and use that saved information at closeout. Add a regression case that replaces the timing report between `waves` and `closeout`.
fix: Closeout recomputes deferral from the current timing report instead of retaining what the fixer was told to skip. If a targeted test run replaces that report with only its own results, a runtime-deferred test without a matching defer flag disappears from closeout, even when its target was edited and the test never ran. Persist the deferred tests and reasons when generating waves, preserve them across follow-up waves, and use that saved information at closeout. Add a regression case that replaces the timing report between `waves` and `closeout`.

minor.name: The new closeout command does not shell-quote its test paths.
minor.summary: Copilot (pullrequestreview-5556332749): The new closeout command does not shell-quote its test paths. For a checkout at `/tmp/my project`, the shell splits each test path into separate arguments, so copying the printed command fails instead of running the deferred suites. Quote each complete path before joining the arguments; this also fixes commands generated for non-deferred tests in fixer briefs.
fix: The new closeout command does not shell-quote its test paths. For a checkout at `/tmp/my project`, the shell splits each test path into separate arguments, so copying the printed command fails instead of running the deferred suites. Quote each complete path before joining the arguments; this also fixes commands generated for non-deferred tests in fixer briefs.

minor.name: closeout deferred-tests block: scope and blocked-run output undocumented
minor.summary:
SKILL.md line 40 and Step 8 (lines 872-874) say closeout prints the deferred tests 'the fixes reach' and frame the block as following the Phase 5 done line. In pr_review.py _cmd_closeout the block is computed from changed_paths(repo, build_head), i.e. every tracked diff plus untracked file since build_head (developer edits and --resolved work included, not only fixer edits), and it is printed after phase5_line() before CaptureError is raised, so a [blocked] closeout also prints it. Rule 5 (lines 837-839) still says the printed line on exit 1 is only the [blocked] line. An agent following Rule 5 may treat the extra stdout block on a blocked run as unexpected, and the 'fixes reach' wording understates what is listed.

Also (roast): The closeout row now says it prints 'any deferred tests the fixes reach' and, in the next sentence, that `--deferred` records a developer-confirmed defer of an issue; pr-fixer.md likewise puts 'Pick, do not defer' directly above 'Never run a deferred test'. A reader of the command table can reasonably think `--deferred` controls the slow-test block.
fix: In SKILL.md Rule 5 (around lines 837-839) add that the deferred tests: block follows the [blocked] line too, and in line 40 / Step 8 say the block covers tests reached by every path changed since build_head (commits, working tree, untracked).

Alternatively change _cmd_closeout in plugins/harness/scripts/pr_review.py to print deferred_lines only when problems is empty, matching the current Step 8 framing, and reword 'the fixes reach' to 'the changes since build_head reach'.

In SKILL.md line 40 write 'then any slow tests held out of the fix waves (the `deferred tests:` block)', and keep `--deferred` as the issue-defer flag; or add '(unrelated to `--deferred`)' after the block mention.

minor.name: Deferred-rule pin is a separate one-assert test next to the existing rules pin
minor.summary: test_fixer_rules_forbid_deferred_tests is a single substring check on _fixer_rules(); TestPathsAndScope.test_fixer_rules_cover_failed_and_out_of_scope (line 1265) already pins rule text from the same function. Two homes for one contract invites drift.
fix: Move the `Never run a test marked deferred` assertion into test_fixer_rules_cover_failed_and_out_of_scope and delete the standalone test.
Or assert the rule inside test_fixer_brief_lists_slow_and_flagged_tests_as_deferred against the rendered brief, so the pin checks the brief a fixer actually reads.

minor.name: Closeout deferral test does not pin the per-test reason lines
minor.summary: test_closeout_prints_deferred_tests_the_fixes_reach checks the header and the single combined pytest line but not the `  - tests/test_flagged.py (properties.super_slow)` / `  - tests/test_slow.py (measured 90 s > 60 s)` lines deferred_lines emits (pr_review.py:1882). Dropping or mislabeling the reasons at closeout would go unnoticed, while the fixer-brief test does pin its reason text.
fix: Assert both reason lines are in `out`, e.g. "  - tests/test_flagged.py (properties.super_slow)" in out and "  - tests/test_slow.py (measured 90 s > 60 s)" in out.
